<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `77f96bf9ed26075008b6d13fd5481ce79e262b0c` — the merge of head `e4b68eb2beb7f03ce580fa4de5d31d53432c8219` into base `159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 77f96bf9ed26075008b6d13fd5481ce79e262b0c && git checkout 77f96bf9ed26075008b6d13fd5481ce79e262b0c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549 e4b68eb2beb7f03ce580fa4de5d31d53432c8219 && git checkout -B drift-repro 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549 && git merge --no-ff e4b68eb2beb7f03ce580fa4de5d31d53432c8219

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e4b68eb2beb7f03ce580fa4de5d31d53432c8219`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-e8-readers.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: packages/objectql/src/metadata-facade.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-lock-state.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-bindings.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/spec/src/system/doc.zod.ts, content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx (the last two on `main`). Not reviewed: .changeset/33264-bare-doc-read-refusal.md and the TSDoc/comments in the diff (prose faces; read only to judge ② and the declaration lines).

Inputs read: card #33264 body and all 6 comments (triage 6880042370, analysis 6893232800, routing 6893248835, ruling 6893582352, claim 6893692442, dev report 6898101382); PR #34036 body, file list (4 files, +168/−1) and the net diff against `main`; the 51 check-runs on the head. #34040 and #34041 are named by the brief and were not opened.

### ① Derived judgments

Gate verdicts: 35 check-runs `success`, 16 `skipped`, none failed or pending on `e4b68eb2be` (Test Core 1/8–8/8, Type Check workspace/source/consumer/debt, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard all green). `mergeable_state: clean`; the three `main` commits since the merge-base that touch the same two source files (0593356f, 68e726d6, a520f550) change no line of `resolveItem`, `readBareDoc` or the doc judge.

Every accept-set and surface change the diff implies:

- D1 — `SchemaRegistry.resolveItem('doc', NAME)` with no caller package, 2 or more ENABLED holders (`packageScopedHoldersOf`), no stamp-less bare-slot entry: FROM `getItem`'s first composite (or the bare/overlay tier) TO a thrown `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `ambiguous-in-environment`, every served holder a candidate). RIGHT — this is ruling 6893582352 option A verbatim. Pinned in both registration orders; ablation A red.
- D2 — same read, exactly one enabled holder beside one or more disabled ones: FROM the first registered (possibly the disabled package's item) TO the enabled holder's item (`getPackageScopedItem`). A served→served move at the registry/facade, not a refusal. RIGHT — the ruling's "a disabled package is not a holder", and the #32183 precedent `packageScopedHoldersOf` already carries. Pinned (ablation C red). It is declared in the PR body table; the changeset files it under its "Unchanged:" paragraph (N3).
- D3 — a caller package (`resolveItem('doc', NAME, PKG)`), one holder, no holder, all holders disabled: straight to `getItem`, byte-for-byte the `main` path. RIGHT; pinned by the CONTROLs.
- D4 — a bare-slot entry carrying no package stamp (absent, empty or `sys_metadata`): answers first via `getItem`, before any holder count. RIGHT — the ruling's environment clause, the same slot `getItem` served first on `main`. Pinned (ablation D red).
- D5 — `MetadataFacade.get` / `getEntry` inherit D1/D2 (both read `registry.resolveItem`, metadata-facade.ts:242/258); `exists` stays `true` (its existing `instanceof PackageScopedNameRefusedError` catch, :305-312). RIGHT; the ruling names the facade explicitly. No in-repo non-test caller of `get('doc', …)` exists to break.
- D6 — `readMetaItem` (served and execution faces), `request.type === 'doc'` after `canonicalizeMetaRequestType`, no `packageId`: the registry judge runs before the draft-preview arm, step 1, the MetadataService and the registry step. So the refusal covers the active read AND the strict `state: 'draft'` / `previewDrafts` reads of a two-holder name. RIGHT — same placement as the `readsByPackage` types (`packagelessScopedRead`) and the action judge, and the bare draft save/publish of that address already refuse. The draft arms are inside the declared class ("a by-name read of a doc that names no package") but carry no pin of their own (noted, not graded).
- D7 — a read naming a package (`?package=`): the judge is skipped (`!request.packageId`), nothing else moves. RIGHT.
- D8 — judge only: when the registry answers, its item is discarded and the layers run as on `main`. RIGHT for this card; its consequence for the environment clause at the REST door is N2.
- D9 — a registry with no `resolveItem` (a host double): the read is silently unjudged and keeps `main`'s answer. Acceptable for a bucket-1 type (the `501` unjudgeable-engine refusal is ruled for buckets 2–4 only).
- D10 — public surface: no schema, no export map, no `index.ts` line moves. `refuseAmbiguousBareDocRead` is a module-level export not re-exported from the package entry; `readBareDoc` is `private`. The only runtime-visible type stretch is `'doc' as PackageScopedResolvableType` on the refusal (N4).
- D11 — SQL: no query added; the judge is one in-memory registry read per bare doc read. No id materialization, no in-app join.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/33264-bare-doc-read-refusal.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` patch, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch — the two packages the diff moves, and no other. RIGHT under AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. `Check Changeset` is green.
- Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` — TRUE of the diff. No accept set of a published schema widens; one answer moves from served to refused. The line is line-initial and identical in the PR body and the changeset. The card body's "Clause-② yes, narrowing" was corrected by routing 6893248835 and the ruling.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — RIGHT, although `packages/metadata-protocol/src` is touched. The line names the kind of change to what a metadata AUTHOR can write, not the package: no key, accepted value, requirement, default or declared meaning of `DocSchema` (or any schema) moves; two packages may still ship one doc name and both still register. What a relative doc link to a two-holder name resolved to was a registration-order pick the spec never declared, so there is no `semantic` kind either. `none` ⇒ `patch` holds.
- Title carries `!` (`fix(objectql)!: …`) — confirmed.
- BREAKING banner — present in the changeset body (`**BREAKING** for a caller that reads a doc by its name alone …` with the one-line fix), where AGENTS.md requires it. The PR body itself carries NO line spelled BREAKING (its `!` title and the Clause-② line carry it there).
- ADR-0087 marker — exactly one, in the changeset body: `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; true of the diff (no key, stored row or export changes shape). The PR body carries none, which is where the rule puts it (changeset body only).
- `Skills-docs:` line — ABSENT from the PR body (and from the changeset). A `(narrowing)` arm owes it (pm-dispatch SKILL.md claim template; review-checklist "缺 ⇒ REWORK"). See N1.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (`deviations` of 6898101382), each answered:

1. Claim said `Clause-②: no`; PR and changeset say `no (narrowing)` — correct, and what the ruling orders.
2. A package-less doc row only the store holds is not exempt — ANSWERED: faithful to ruling A and no wider than the declared narrowing; reasoning in ④.
3. `registry.ts` carries the import line, the one-line `resolveItem` branch and the new private method, against the claim's "one minimal hunk" — accepted; nothing else in the file moves.
4. `origin/main` merged once, later action-scoped commits not re-merged — accepted; verified above that they touch no line of this seam and GitHub reports `clean`.
5. Full suites ran before the cost rule — no effect on the record.

`open_questions`: empty.

`out_of_scope_findings`: the two class-a readings (`?package=` on a composed server answering the other package's doc; one holder disabled and registered last answering `404` at the REST doors) are, per the brief, filed as #34040 and #34041 — not opened here; the first one bears on this PR's own BREAKING prescription (N5). Two carriers the ruling names have no card number in any input I was given and are ESCALATED to the seat: the `domain:skills` card for the ADR-0048 status-line edit, and the UI-lane follow-up for Console `/docs/NAME` showing the candidates on a 409.

Author note: PR `user.login` is the fleet relay; nothing to name.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`. `packages/spec/src/system/doc.zod.ts` (header) declares the capability: two packages MAY ship a doc under one bare name and "each resolves within its own package", by `getItem('doc', name, packageId)` / `?package=` on the detail route. It declares nothing about what a read naming no package answers for such a name. `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx` ("Addressing an item by its package") already publishes the other half for `/meta`: "The server picks no holder for you. A bare name that two packages hold … is answered `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`." So this change takes no declared capability away at the consumer: the package-named read is untouched (D3, D7), and the bare read moves from an undeclared registration-order pick to the refusal the published page already states. It makes the spec's own refusal real. `doc` stays in ADR-0150 D1 bucket 1: no `PACKAGE_SCOPED_TYPES` edit, no closure rule, no new address form — the option-B reclassification the ruling rejected is not smuggled in.

The seam holds against the cited code. One judge (`readBareDoc`) and two askers is the right shape: the dev's measurement that the composed REST read never reached the registry for this answer (the MetadataService copy at step 2 precedes the registry at step 3) is consistent with `readMetaItem`'s layer order as read, so a registry-only judge would have missed the REST door and a protocol-only one the facade.

The reading the dev flags — a store-only package-less row is not exempt. Faithful, for three reasons read off the tree:

- `doc` is a SEALED type (`SEALED_ROW_SERVED_OVERRIDE_TYPES`, protocol-package-bindings.ts; ADR-0131 D6). `declinesStoredRow` (protocol-lock-state.ts) declines every stored row of a name a managed package ships except the shipping package's declared `.custom` override, so step 1 of the read does not adopt a package-less row under a two-holder name. On `main` that row therefore never answered this read from the store; the ruling's "the environment's own saved row STILL answers first" preserves an answer, and here there is none to preserve.
- Exempting it would not serve the row; it would hand the read back to steps 2–3, i.e. to the registration-order pick the ruling abolishes (the dev measured exactly that: `200`, last-registered holder).
- It is not wider than the declaration: the refused set is still exactly {no package named} × {2 or more enabled holders} × {no stamp-less bare-slot entry}, all inside "a name two or more enabled packages hold". A stored row does not lower the holder count.

Attempts to break it, and what they found:

- Hydrated row vs store-only row (same stored row, before and after a boot). `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` does register a package-less doc row in the bare slot (`declinesBorrowedEnvelope` passes a package-less row; `loadMetaFromDb` skips only objects), but for an unscoped type it grafts the envelope of `lookupArtifactItem(type, name, undefined)` — the first-registered holder's `_packageId` — through `mergeArtifactProtection`. `readBareDoc`'s exemption tests the stamp, so by my reading such a hydrated row is NOT taken for the environment's own and the read refuses `409`, the same answer as the pinned store-only case. That is consistent, and on the refusal side; but it is read, not measured, it has no pin, and it contradicts the new TSDoc's "(its package-less bare slot: a hydrated or saved row)" (N2).
- Environment clause at the REST door. The exemption is honoured where the judge sits (registry, facade). Because the protocol only asks the judge (D8), a stamp-less bare entry beside two holders on a server whose MetadataService holds a holder's copy leaves the answer to step 2, as on `main`. The in-diff CONTROL pins `env doc` at the protocol only with no service copy. Not a regression and not a widening; unmeasured on the composed rig (N2).
- `/layers` and `/published`. `getMetaItemLayered` itself is not judged; the two REST doors refuse because they read the plain item first (`runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`, `rest-server.ts`), as the dev measured. Correct today, pinned nowhere in this diff, and an in-process `getMetaItemLayered` naming no package still answers one holder's code layer (N6).
- Disabled holders, three holders, a caller package, the plural spelling, a named member (`doc` has no discriminator): no path found that refuses outside the declared class or serves a disabled package's item at the registry.

Findings:

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — the PR body lacks the `Skills-docs:` line a `(narrowing)` arm owes. Prose face (PR body edit, the head does not move); the lane seat's ACCEPT checklist makes it a rework of the body before ACCEPT. A true line here is likely `none — REASON` for skills, with `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx` already teaching the `/meta` 409 and the ADR-0048 status line owed by its own card.
- N2 (nit) — the environment clause is pinned only for a stamp-less bare entry with no service copy. Follow-up card: on the composed rig, read (a) a hydrated package-less doc row beside two holders and (b) a stamp-less bare entry beside two holders with a service copy, at the facade and both REST transports, pin what answers, and make the TSDoc sentence "a hydrated or saved row" say what is measured (TSDoc is a prose face).
- N3 (nit) — the changeset's "Unchanged:" paragraph holds the sentence "the facade serves the enabled holder's doc", which is a move (D2), as the PR body table states correctly. Prose face.
- N4 (nit) — `type: 'doc' as PackageScopedResolvableType` places a value outside the exported union in `refusal.type`. No reader in the tree switches on it beyond `typeLabel`'s default arm; accepted deviation, or a follow-up widening the refusal's type in `@objectstack/core`.
- N5 (nit) — the BREAKING banner's one-line fix is "name the package (`?package=PACKAGE_ID` on the REST door)". The dev's own out-of-scope reading says that on a composed artifact server this address answers the OTHER package's doc, on `main` and here. The gap is pre-existing, not narrowed by this PR, and carried by its own card (per the brief, one of #34040/#34041); the seat should sequence or cross-reference it so the prescription the changelog ships is one that works. Prose face / follow-up.
- N6 (nit) — no pin for the `409` at `/layers` and `/published`, which depends on those doors reading the plain item first. Follow-up card.

Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jRMKz5NhWVrE4E1U5x`

One holder, a read naming the package, and the environment's own bare-slot item are all unchanged. This makes the refusal `client-sdk.mdx` already publishes real, rather than taking a declared capability away.

Add a true line. `none — <reason>` is likely right, since `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx` already teaches the `/meta` 409; if anything is owed, file it and name it `#N`. - N2/N6 (follow-up card): there are no pins for a hydrated package-less row or for a stamp-less bare entry with a service copy beside two holders on the composed rig, and none for the 409 at `/layers` and `/published`. The TSDoc "a hydrated or saved row" goes beyond what is measured.
- Escalated to the seat: ruling 6893582352 names two follow-up carriers that have no card number yet, the `domain:skills` ADR-0048 status-line card and the UI-lane Console `/docs/NAME` 409-candidates card.

## 席位核对

Verdict: **ACCEPT** · head `e4b68eb2beb7f03ce580fa4de5d31d53432c8219` · area S5 lands it (not governed)

- Shape: `Fixes #33264`. Ruling 6893582352, option A. 4 files, +169/−1. `check-governed-merges`: not governed, under 3000 lines.
- Premise measured: the dev measured on a composed artifact server at main (report 6898101382). The REST bare read answered the last-registered holder from the MetadataService copy, so one judge asked from the protocol covers both doors.
- Review: review-c's ACCEPT read is PASS (6898681116, body re-read at this head). The CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER record 6898579083 is PASS with no must-fix and no should-fix. Rework 6898586827 (Skills-docs line) is addressed in the body.
- Gates: 59 check-runs at this head (with the body re-runs), 39 success and 20 skipped, none red. Mergeable `clean`.
- Accepted deviations:
  - The claim's `Clause-②: no` is corrected in the PR and changeset to `no (narrowing)`, with `!`, a BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 marker and a dogfood battery at this head.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is left to CI, where it is green.
